units.title: Construct: Single-evaluation propagation and atomic parser publication
steps: Explain which failure stage owns the error offset, and why early-return propagation is not transaction rollback or automatic cleanup.
Implement strict checked accumulation and two single-evaluation propagation forms without statement expressions, strto* or parser libraries.
checks: 1:65534 succeeds with 65535. 65536:0 fails RANGE at offset4; 1:2x fails INVALID at3; 1: fails at2; :1 fails at0. 1:65535 fails RANGE at7 and must not publish the first field.

Generate all strings of length0–6 over digits0,1,9,colon,x and compare with an independent grammar/integer model. Add UINT32 bounds and long zero prefixes. Record callback/expression counters to kill double evaluation and retain a canary output for every rejection; kill premature publication and trailing-input acceptance mutants.
reasoning: Explain which failure stage owns the error offset, and why early-return propagation is not transaction rollback or automatic cleanup.
deliverables: Implement strict checked accumulation and two single-evaluation propagation forms without statement expressions, strto* or parser libraries.

Replace the complete buffer with two incremental segments and preserve an explicit consumed position. steps: Derive a state table in which progress and terminal/error status are independent, and distinguish accepted bytes from durable bytes.
Implement a one-call bounded adapter with overflow-free relative-to-absolute progress conversion and explicit borrowed-buffer lifetime.
checks: With length4,next0 and backend (2,AGAIN), return (2,AGAIN). Retrying from2 with (1,IO) returns (3,IO). A backend count2 offered only one byte violates the contract and returns the original next. Empty input does not call the sink.

Assert call counts, offered spans, no retry duplication and unchanged next on contract violations. Kill error-discards-progress and status-erasure mutants. Use a separate actual pipe adapter only as an additional OS experiment.
